title: Plugin Extension Onramp: Lightweight Developer Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose
--------
Quick, pragmatic playbook to help a backend/frontend/infra engineer ship a tiny Redwood plugin extension that hooks into the SDK surface (hooks for auth, telemetry, and sample routing). This is explicitly a lightweight path: zero heavy infra changes, minimal configuration, reproducible locally and in CI.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-first-success for plugin authors to < 2 hours.
- Provide a scaffold + test harness for local iteration and CI smoke tests.
- Define telemetry & contract expectations so integrations don't regress.
- Surface common failure modes and recovery patterns (latency, auth, cache).

Audience
- Platform engineers who need to add a new plugin (metrics exporter, custom auth, model selector).
- SDK maintainers reviewing PRs.
- Solutions engineers prototyping customer integrations.

What counts as a "plugin" here
- A small package (JS/TS or Go) that implements one or more well-defined extension points in the SDK runtime: pre-request hook, post-response hook, auth provider, routing policy, or a tiny caching layer.
- Runs sidecar or as part of the host process (we prioritize in-process for dev loops).

Quickstart (10–90 min path)
1) bootstrap: repo clone + scaffold
   - git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/plugin-stub.git && cd plugin-stub
   - ./scripts/new-plugin.sh --name my-telemetry-plugin --lang ts
   - opens a minimal package with: index.ts, README.md, tests/, ci/
2) run locally against sandbox runtime
   - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=dev-local-xxx
   - yarn install && yarn start:dev (starts a tiny host runtime + plugin loader)
   - open http://localhost:7000/health and http://localhost:7000/debug/plugins
3) smoke test flow (~5 min)
   - run yarn test:integration (loads plugin, sends a sample request, verifies metrics emitted and no error)
4) PR checklist & reviewers
   - add a small README with config knobs
   - add a telemetry contract test (see below)
   - assign eng-developer-experience and the relevant runtime owner

Minimal plugin API contract (must implement one or more)
- preRequest(ctx): optionally mutate request, return {continue: true|false}
- postResponse(ctx, resp): inspect logs, send enrichments
- init(config): return teardown() optionally
- getMetadata(): {name, version, author}

Telemetry contract (non-negotiable)
- Every plugin must emit structured events for the three lifecycle points: plugin.init, plugin.request, plugin.teardown (if used).
- Events must include: plugin_name, plugin_version, correlation_id (from SDK request_ctx), elapsed_ms (where applicable).
- We prefer JSON-line stdout in dev; CI asserts the presence and shape.

Local test harness
- test/integration/smoke.spec.ts: starts a headless runtime, wires plugin into a sandbox model stub, asserts telemetry lines and no uncaught errors.
- test/mocks/model-stub.js: deterministic responses for latency/edge-case testing (e.g., long-token sequence, early OOM simulation).
- CI configuration runs smoke tests on each PR with matrix: node 18, node 20, linux, darwin.

Config surface (keep small)
- PLUGIN_ENABLED=true
- PLUGIN_MODE=inline | isolated (inline default for dev)
- PLUGIN_LOG_LEVEL=info|debug|error
- PLUGIN_ENDPOINT_URL (if the plugin proxies to external service)

Failure modes & mitigations (notes to self)
- Plugin throws during init: runtime should mark plugin unhealthy and continue without it (error reported, admin alert). Add tests to simulate thrown init.
- Plugin mutates request into invalid shape: SDK must validate request schema after preRequest and reject safely. Add schema fixture tests.
- Network calls in plugin are slow: plugin should use timeouts and circuit breakers; default timeout = 250ms for preRequest hooks in hosted quickpath.

Security checklist
- No secrets in plugin repo. If plugin needs secrets, read from REDWOOD_PLUGIN_SECRET_{NAME} which is set via platform secret manager in Dedicated/Private.
- Plugins run in a restricted process environment when deployed to Dedicated/Private (draft policy: drop NET_ADMIN, disable ptrace).

Review & rollout plan (minimal)
- Stage: dev -> canary (5% traffic, dedicated test cluster) -> gradual rollout 25/50/100.
- KPI signals to watch during canary: 95th latency delta, error rate, increase in token cost (if plugin triggers additional model calls).

Contrib guidelines for SDK maintainers (how to review)
- Does plugin implement minimal contract? (init, pre/post hooks, metadata)
- Is telemetry schema present and tested?
- Are timeouts and aborts respected? (simulate slow external call in tests)
- Is the README clear about how to run locally and how to configure in Dedicated/Private?

Open questions / TODOs
- Decide default timeout for postResponse hooks (currently undecided). Proposal: 500ms for postResponse, 200ms for preRequest. (action: @Ethan)
- Confirm isolation policy for on-prem deployments (how to safely load third-party plugin binaries). (action: security team)
- Determine whether we allow plugins to trigger additional model calls during hooks (cost implications). Quick suggestion: allow but require an explicit flag and cost tags.

Appendix: example minimal TypeScript preRequest hook (pseudo)
// index.ts
async function init(config){
  // set up client, metrics, etc
  return async function teardown(){ /* noop */ }
}

async function preRequest(ctx){
  const start = Date.now();
  if(ctx.request.headers['x-ignore-plugin']) return {continue: true};
  ctx.request.prompt = sanitizePrompt(ctx.request.prompt);
  emitTelemetry({event: 'plugin.request', plugin: 'my-telemetry-plugin', correlation_id: ctx.correlation_id, elapsed_ms: Date.now()-start});
  return {continue: true};
}

module.exports = {init, preRequest, getMetadata: ()=>({name:'my-telemetry-plugin', version:'0.1.0'})};

---
Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally opinionated and short. If this path works we can convert into a short workshop lab (30–45m) for new hires and a reproducible template in the SDK repo.

Last checkins
- 2025-01-20: paired with Ethan to add telemetry tester harness.
- 2025-02-06: added CI matrix and updated smoke tests to assert telemetry shape.
